title: Ukraine Deploys Hundreds of AI Turrets to Fight 800 km/h Drones
summary:
Defense Minister Yevhen Khmara announced a massive expansion of automated gun systems in Ukraine's air defense network to target fast moving Russian aircraft. The ministry is deploying hundreds of large caliber robotic turrets and tasking domestic manufacturers to develop versions capable of intercepting drones traveling at 800 km/h. This rollout integrates automated weapons into a multi layered defense involving surface to air missiles, man portable systems and electronic warfare.

The Air Force recently confirmed the first shootdown of a Geran-5 jet drone using a Sky Sentinel turret equipped with a 12.7 mm machine gun and AI assisted targeting. President Volodymyr Zelensky deployed 12 such systems in Kyiv with 8 more planned for the region, although a presidential adviser called them a final line of defense rather than a city wide shield. Some social media reports from the capital allege that these defenses can inadvertently endanger civilians during engagements.

selectedTweets.bestBit: Ukraine has hundreds of large-caliber turrets in its air defense system for intercepting jet-powered drones
selectedTweets.text: ❗️Ukraine has hundreds of large-caliber turrets in its air defense system for intercepting jet-powered drones, as stated by Defense Minister Yevhen Khmara. The turrets have already demonstrated effectiveness against Russian jet-powered UAVs, and this direction is planned to be scaled up within a multi-layered air defense system (SAM systems, MANPADS, turrets, EW, interceptor drone crews, and aviation). The Ministry of Defense is increasing the number of turrets, developing longer-range systems, and preparing for new Russian drones with speeds of around 800 km/h, assigning corresponding tasks to Ukrainian manufacturers.

selectedTweets.bestBit: Ukraine has shot down a jet-powered Geran-5 drone using a robotic turret for the first time
selectedTweets.text:
🤖 Ukraine has shot down a jet-powered Geran-5 drone using a robotic turret for the first time

The claim was made by Ukrainian Air Force spokesman Yurii Ihnat.

The turrets use machine vision and AI-assisted targeting to calculate a drone’s trajectory and aim the weapon. Ihnat said he had initially been skeptical that a machine-gun system could effectively engage such fast targets. For now, the main limitation is its relatively short range.

The day before, Zelensky said more than 12 such turrets have already been deployed in Kyiv, including to protect bridges, with another eight planned for the Kyiv region. The systems are automated mounts equipped with heavy machine guns.
